_about: The narration of the batnet film, one scene per entry. `text` is spoken (ElevenLabs); `caption` is what the subtitles show, in plain English; `pad` is the pause after it, in seconds; `min` is the scene's least length. Spellings like 'ze', 'ven', 'willage', 'ewery' and 'unt' are on purpose: the narrator has a thick German accent. The 'Allo 'Allo! and Dad's Army lines are on purpose too. Scenes in scenes.js key their moments to phrases of `text` (cue()), so a phrase quoted there must stay in the text. Edit here, then `python3 video/render.py` (see video/README.md).

scenes.text: batnet. Ven ze grid goes down, ze willage keeps talking.
scenes.caption: batnet. When the grid goes down, the village keeps talking.

scenes.text: Berlin, September last year. One fire at ze foot of two pylons in Johannisthal, unt fifty sousand homes unt businesses go dark for two unt a half days. No light, no trams, no traffic lights, unt after a few hours no mobile netvork: ze masts haff batteries for exactly long enough to be useless. Put zat light out! Ah. Nobody needs to say it. Zis is not a film. Zis happened.
scenes.caption: Berlin, September last year. One fire at the foot of two pylons in Johannisthal, and fifty thousand homes and businesses go dark for two and a half days. No light, no trams, no traffic lights, and after a few hours no mobile network: the masts have batteries for exactly long enough to be useless. Put that light out! Ah. Nobody needs to say it. This is not a film. This happened.

scenes.text: Now imagine ewery sird house has a small radio node. Ze lights are out, but ze street is talking: who has a generator, vhich pharmacy is open, who needs insulin. Ze messages hop from house to house, like gossip, but faster.
scenes.caption: Now imagine every third house has a small radio node. The lights are out, but the street is talking: who has a generator, which pharmacy is open, who needs insulin. The messages hop from house to house, like gossip, but faster.

scenes.text: Ewery house: one Raspberry Pi, ze size of a packet of cigarettes, on a power bank. It makes an open Vee-Fee. Your own phone joins, iPhone or Android, opens ze browser, unt zere is a chat app. Nossing to install. Like VatsApp, but no internet, no account, no company. Who are you? Don't tell him, Pike! Only your neighbour approves you. Houses link to each ozer over Vee-Fee mesh, unt over ze hills by LoRa radio. Listen wery carefully, I shall say zis only vunce: ze willage key is a QR code on ze admin's phone.
scenes.caption: Every house: one Raspberry Pi, the size of a packet of cigarettes, on a power bank. It makes an open WiFi. Your own phone joins, iPhone or Android, opens the browser, and there is a chat app. Nothing to install. Like WhatsApp, but no internet, no account, no company. Who are you? Don't tell him, Pike! Only your neighbour approves you. Houses link to each other over WiFi mesh, and over the hills by LoRa radio. Listen very carefully, I shall say this only once: the village key is a QR code on the admin's phone.

scenes.text: Vhy two radios? Vee-Fee is fast: it carries calls, voice messages unt photos, but only a few hundred metres. LoRa is slow, about one sousand bits a second, but it goes one to sree kilometres on less power zan your phone, no licence needed. A short text is half a second on air. Voice? Impossible. So ze house turns your voice into text in a quarter of a second, sends ze text, unt ze ozer end reads it aloud. Ze radio can hide under ze bed, like in ze café. No flashing knobs.
scenes.caption: Why two radios? WiFi is fast: it carries calls, voice messages and photos, but only a few hundred metres. LoRa is slow, about one thousand bits a second, but it goes one to three kilometres on less power than your phone, no licence needed. A short text is half a second on air. Voice? Impossible. So the house turns your voice into text in a quarter of a second, sends the text, and the other end reads it aloud. The radio can hide under the bed, like in the café. No flashing knobs.

scenes.text: Vhat does it cost? A Raspberry Pi Zero: nineteen euros. A LoRa radio module: twenty-five. Zat is it. Under fifty euros for a radio station in your pocket, on ze power bank you already own, for a day unt a half. A house node, vith Vee-Fee for ze vhole street unt sixty phones: about one hundred unt fifty. Ja, estimates: ve haff not measured zem yet. Ve are not stupid boys.
scenes.caption: What does it cost? A Raspberry Pi Zero: nineteen euros. A LoRa radio module: twenty-five. That is it. Under fifty euros for a radio station in your pocket, on the power bank you already own, for a day and a half. A house node, with WiFi for the whole street and sixty phones: about one hundred and fifty. Yes, estimates: we have not measured them yet. We are not stupid boys.

scenes.text: Does it need ze internet? No. Nossing leaves ze willage. Do I need an app? No, any browser. How many people? About sixty phones per house node, eight on a pocket node. How long on a battery? A pocket node: a day unt a half on a power bank. A house node: sree days on a car battery. Is it legal? Ja. A licence-free band, low power, unt ve keep to ze rules. Who can read my messages? Your willage only: zey are sealed vith ze willage key. Can strangers join? Only if a neighbour approves zem. My house loses power? Ze ozer houses keep copies; you catch up ven you are back. Photos, calls? Over Vee-Fee, ja. Over ze long radio, text only.
scenes.caption: Does it need the internet? No. Nothing leaves the village. Do I need an app? No, any browser. How many people? About sixty phones per house node, eight on a pocket node. How long on a battery? A pocket node: a day and a half on a power bank. A house node: three days on a car battery. Is it legal? Yes. A licence-free band, low power, and we keep to the rules. Who can read my messages? Your village only: they are sealed with the village key. Can strangers join? Only if a neighbour approves them. My house loses power? The other houses keep copies; you catch up when you are back. Photos, calls? Over WiFi, yes. Over the long radio, text only.

scenes.text: Glastonbury. Two hundred sousand people, one hill, unt a mobile netvork zat surrenders by Friday lunchtime. Ve're doomed! Doomed! No. Pocket nodes on power banks, one per camp, linked by radio across ze fields. Each one passes ze message to ze next: sree hops, unt ze vhole farm is covered. Ze first messages: Oasis are playing a secret gig. Zey are not. Unt somebody is robbing tents in field seven. Zey are.
scenes.caption: Glastonbury. Two hundred thousand people, one hill, and a mobile network that surrenders by Friday lunchtime. We're doomed! Doomed! No. Pocket nodes on power banks, one per camp, linked by radio across the fields. Each one passes the message to the next: three hops, and the whole farm is covered. The first messages: Oasis are playing a secret gig. They are not. And somebody is robbing tents in field seven. They are.

scenes.text: A child is lost near ze stage. Ze message is marked High: it jumps ze queue on ze radio, unt reaches ewery camp in under a minute. Ja, ewery camp.
scenes.caption: A child is lost near the stage. The message is marked High: it jumps the queue on the radio, and reaches every camp in under a minute. Yes, every camp.

scenes.text: Zen: a bang, somevhere by ze vest field. Don't panic! Don't panic! Nobody panics: ewerybody reports it, ewerybody sees ze reports, so nobody runs ze vrong vay, unt ze medics see exactly vhere to go. Each report costs half a second of airtime; ze rules allow six minutes an hour. Plenty.
scenes.caption: Then: a bang, somewhere by the west field. Don't panic! Don't panic! Nobody panics: everybody reports it, everybody sees the reports, so nobody runs the wrong way, and the medics see exactly where to go. Each report costs half a second of airtime; the rules allow six minutes an hour. Plenty.

scenes.text: Ve do not guess. Ve are wery sorough. Ze real code runs in a simulator: forty houses, a bang, two hundred unt forty-seven posts, ewery one delivered, twelve milliseconds in ze middle. Ewery message is signed vith ze house's own key, so nobody can fake your neighbour. Clocks? Ve do not trust zem: messages are ordered by a logical clock, so a Pi vith ze vrong time still agrees vith ze street. Zen ve take it to ze field.
scenes.caption: We do not guess. We are very thorough. The real code runs in a simulator: forty houses, a bang, two hundred and forty-seven posts, every one delivered, twelve milliseconds in the middle. Every message is signed with the house's own key, so nobody can fake your neighbour. Clocks? We do not trust them: messages are ordered by a logical clock, so a Pi with the wrong time still agrees with the street. Then we take it to the field.

scenes.text: batnet. Open source, cheap, unt it vorks ven nossing else does. Ve haff vays of making you talk... to your neighbours. Good moaning.
scenes.caption: batnet. Open source, cheap, and it works when nothing else does. We have ways of making you talk... to your neighbours. Good moaning.
